summary: Extended the compaction lead to the other producer the trim child's discriminator names, using sources rather than another execution. OmniPaxos bounds a user-supplied snapshot index by the leader's decided index (an index equal to it is mapped to the decided log without the StopSign, a lower index is used as given, a greater one is refused with the decided index reported) and then builds the snapshot from the storage range starting at the current compacted index — neither bound nor range is tied to what a replica actually holds, and the same investigation witnesses the decided index drifting above the content, so a snapshot request could be accepted past the entries and store a snapshot created from an empty range while advancing the compacted index, after which readers of that region would see the snapshot instead of the entries. Registered for this: three sources (the documented note on the snapshot caller, try_snapshot's decided-index comparison, and create_snapshot's range), a behaviour recording that the snapshot bound comes from the decided index alone, and a child question under the drift parent whose hypothesis and discriminator spell out the decisive observations (the call's result, the reported compacted index, and what a read of the region returns for each node before and after). The child interpretation is source-only with conclusion and defect_claim unresolved, keeping the counterevidence explicit: no snapshot call has been executed after a drift, and in the sampled drifted states the StopSign adjustment of the equal case lowered the effective bound, so only strictly-lower requests would escape it; its limitations note the dependence on the entry type's Snapshot implementation and the unanalysed forwarding to peers. No execution was requested this turn; incomplete are the snapshot-after-drift probe, the underflow/other-producer questions for trim, the parent drift's bound and reconfiguration-handoff questions, timers and loss triggers, larger clusters, persistence, and any further independent lead.
